title: Best payroll software in the UK (2026): PAYE, pensions and small business payroll

sections.content: Payroll software helps UK employers calculate wages, PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and payslips. This guide explains what small businesses should compare before choosing payroll software, especially if they are hiring staff for the first time.

sections.title: 1. What payroll software should do
sections.content: Good payroll software should calculate pay, deductions, tax, National Insurance and pension contributions. It should also produce payslips, support Real Time Information submissions to HMRC and keep records organised for the business.

sections.title: 2. PAYE and HMRC submissions
sections.content: UK employers usually need to report payroll information to HMRC through Real Time Information. When comparing software, check whether it supports the submissions your business needs and whether it is suitable for your company size.

sections.title: 3. Auto-enrolment pension support
sections.content: If you employ staff, pension duties can become part of payroll. Look for software that can calculate pension contributions, produce reports and work with your chosen pension provider.

sections.title: 4. Small business features to compare
sections.content: Compare monthly price, employee limits, accountant access, payslip delivery, holiday pay support, director payroll, contractor handling, integrations with accounting software and support quality.

sections.title: 5. Payroll software versus accountant payroll
sections.content: Some businesses prefer software because it gives them control. Others use an accountant or payroll bureau to reduce admin. The right option depends on staff numbers, confidence, budget and how complex the payroll is.

sections.title: Can a small business run payroll itself?
sections.content: Yes, many small businesses run payroll themselves using software. However, mistakes can create HMRC and employee problems, so some employers still prefer accountant or bureau support.

sections.title: Does payroll software replace an accountant?
sections.content: Not always. Payroll software can handle calculations and submissions, but an accountant may still help with tax planning, accounts, payroll setup and complex employment situations.
